messages.subject: strong priors for parameter equality?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ed

Hope you and your family are doing well

Could it be possible to use the approach of strong priors (like in cross-loadings) for parameter equalities?

I am thinking it like for measurement invariance, because if we do the label equality, it estimates 1 parameter for both loadings (for example)
mod <- 'f1 =~ c(L1,L1)*x1 + c(L2,L2)*x2 + c(L3,L3)*x3'

But following the logic like using cross-loadings, we could specified that the equality is based on a strong prior, so that if the parameter moves away from the equality would be an indication that invariance doesnt hold, I was thinking something like this:
mod <- 'f1 =~ c(L1,L2)*x1 + c(L3,L4)*x2 + c(L5,L6)*x3
L2 == L1 + a1
L4 == L3 + a2
L6 == L5 + a3
a1 ~ dnorm(0,100)
a2 ~ dnorm(0,100)
a3 ~ dnorm(0,100)'

make sense?

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mauricio,

It seems like a reasonable possibility. I think you can do this now in two steps: first run the model with do.fit=FALSE to figure out the names of the parameters in JAGS. Then set priors with some help from the jagextra argument. Something like this (I am using development version here, but hopefully it runs in the CRAN version as well):

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3 '

## check JAGS parameter names
fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, std.lv=TRUE, do.fit=FALSE)
with(parTable(fit), cbind(lhs,op,rhs,pxnames))

## prior loadings have mean L1, which is set equal to the
## first loading in jagextra argument
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + prior("dnorm(L1,100)")*x2 + prior("dnorm(L1,100)")*x3 '
fit2 <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, std.lv=TRUE, jagextra=list(syntax="L1 <- lambda[1,1,1]"))

You'll get a warning about being unable to compute marginal log-likelihood, but this isn't a big deal.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: path diagram for blavaan
messages.body_plain:
There is no built-in support for path diagrams in blavaan. But blavaan objects are built on lavaan objects, so any functionality for lavaan models might also apply to blavaan models. For example, I believe the semPlot package will work with lavaan models. If you had a blavaan object called "fit", then I would try this command:

class(fit) <- "lavaan"
